newsitem.title: USA: Continental pilots threaten holiday-season strike.
newsitem.headline: Continental pilots threaten holiday-season strike.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. pilots Monday threatened a strike during this year's peak holiday travel season if they are unable to come to terms on a new contract with the carrier.

But industry analysts said it was unlikely federal mediators would allow them to break off talks that quickly, and a Continental spokesman said the carrier still expected to come to terms with the union before an Oct. 1 deadline.

"The (pilots') public comments don't reflect the tonality of the negotiations at the table. There is a real can-do attitude at the table among the negotiating teams," Continental spokesman Ned Walker said.

Negotiators with the Independent Association of Continental Pilots and the Houston-based carrier were set to resume talks in Florida on Tuesday with a federal mediator overseeing the contract bargaining sessions.

The talks, which opened in April, have so far focused on scheduling and other contract terms. The two sides have yet to hash out a union demand for up to 40 percent wage hikes they say would bring the pilots' pay up to the industry average.

"The only thing that separates them is dollars and cents," said Salomon Brothers airline analyst Julius Maldutis. "I'm confident that an agreement will be reached that essentially satisfies all parties."

According to figures released by the airline, the typical Continental captain is paid about $134,000 a year, a pilot receives about $104,000 and a first officer $84,000. That's about 10 percent to 15 percent below the average for the 10 largest domestic airlines.

But Continental has been making up ground on rival carriers. Its pilots received 18.5 percent wage increases and $30 million in lump sum payouts over the past two years under the expired contract, along with regular profit-sharing payouts from the airline, Walker said.

"The average Continental pilot has seen his or her compensation increase by about 25 percent in the last 24 months," he said. "We're very confident we'll have a contract with the pilots during the third quarter."
While negotiations between Continental and its pilots resume this week, talks with the company's Continental Express pilots were "virtually at a standstill," union President Len Nikolai said.
"We're going to take a job action before the year is out" if the two sides fail to sign a new pact by Oct. 1, said Nikolai, a Boeing 737 captain and 31-year Continental pilot.

Union negotiators in late September plan to assess the progress of the talks, and could ask to be released from federal mediation if a new pact is not signed by Oct. 1, Nikolai said during informational picketing that began Monday at Houston's Bush Intercontinental Airport.

If they are allowed to break off the talks, the pilots likely would mount a series of small-scale work stoppages expected to disrupt travel during the peak holiday season after a 30-day cooling off period, he said.
